_note: The consultation toolkit, 2 October 2026. The founder asked for the live triage screen, with the simulated devices, in front of the nurse and the doctor when they consult a patient, linked on the virtual consultation screens with every online tool they need while consulting, and for doctors' notes, sick notes and referrals to be written there. Every tool in this file already existed as a page of its own; what this contract adds is one place in the consultation where the clinician reaches each of them without leaving the call or the visit, in an order per role, and the sentences said where a tool is refused. Nothing here is a real service: each tool keeps its own capability notice from packages/catalog/capabilities.json and its own refusals, and the toolkit adds no act of its own. Which party may use a tool is packages/catalog/vetting.json's, asked live for the clinician on the screen; what the line allows a doctor to decide is packages/catalog/teleconsult.json#clinicalLimits; the patient's devices are packages/catalog/live-vitals.json's board, unchanged.

tools.name: The patient’s devices
tools.summary: Every instrument in the kit and the patient’s own watch, live and simulated, each reading with its source, its age and where it stands against the record’s range.

tools.name: Consultation notes
tools.summary: The consultation record every encounter writes into, as SOAP or in full, with the diagnosis field that is a doctor’s alone.

tools.name: Prescribe
tools.summary: A prescription from the formulary, with the interaction check’s answer read and ticked before it is written.

tools.name: Order tests
tools.summary: A laboratory request, by mode, acknowledged only by the clinician who ordered it when the result arrives.

tools.name: Referral letter
tools.summary: A referral letter to a kind of unit, carrying the reason, the readings and the registration, and nothing else from the file.

tools.name: Sick note
tools.summary: A certificate of unfitness for work, signed under the doctor’s registration, for the days the doctor decides.

tools.name: Patient context
tools.summary: The patient’s file — history, medicines, results, referrals — each section opened only as far as vetting allows the reader.

tools.name: Protocols and guidance
tools.summary: The protocol registry, the record’s indicative ranges and who may decide what — every protocol still a draft.

tools.name: Assessment and readings
tools.summary: The visit assessment: the readings, how each was taken, what you found, and your sign-off — the thing this visit is handed over against.

tools.name: Case pathway
tools.summary: The cases GilbertOne gathered: take one, decide where the patient is seen, repeat a reading, and ask the doctor.

tools.name: Notes for the doctor
tools.summary: The same consultation record, on a nurse’s form: what you found and what concerns you, with no diagnosis field, because a nurse’s assessment is not one.

tools.name: Call a doctor in
tools.summary: A doctor on a call into this room, with you as the examination: what you will see and hear, and what the doctor may decide on the line you have.

tools.name: Refer to a doctor
tools.summary: This visit, handed to the doctors’ review queue once its readings are attached and signed off.

_toolsNote: A tool is one thing a clinician does in a consultation, the screen that already does it, and the vetting capability it asks for. `drawnBy: tool` means the tool's own screen renders its capability notice, so the toolkit does not draw a second copy; `drawnBy: toolkit` means the toolkit draws it above the tool. `decision` marks the tools that decide something about the patient — on a call those wait for a line that allows a decision, and after one they need the encounter to have counted as a consultation. `signsAfterCall` marks the record: written during the call, signed only once the call has ended as a consultation, and closed for an encounter that did not count as one. `onCall` names a teleconsult.json clinical limit the tool needs on a call and the teleconsult.json refusal said, word for word, when the room does not give it: nothing is started and no certificate is written for a patient nobody in the room has examined. `screens` is the evidence, per platform, of the screen the tool opens; null means the platform says what the tool is and who may use it, and opens nothing. `pending` is a tool whose screen is still being built: it is listed, and says so, rather than missing — the sick note was, until packages/catalog/sick-note.json landed the same day with its own capability, issue-medical-certificate, and its own refusals, which its composer draws.

refused.sentence: A nurse does not prescribe on MyThuso. A prescription is written under a doctor’s registration and a separately verified prescribing authority, so a medicine you think is needed goes to the doctor in your notes or on a call.
A nurse does not write a sick note on MyThuso. The certificate is signed under a doctor’s registration once a doctor has reviewed what you found, so ask for one in your notes for the doctor.
A nurse does not order a test on MyThuso. A test is requested by the doctor who will read the result, so a test you think is needed goes to the doctor in your notes.

A nurse does not refer a patient onward from here. A referral letter carries a doctor’s registration to the clinician receiving it; from the house you hand the visit to a doctor, or advise the clinic or the emergency department now.

_surfacesNote: A surface is a consultation screen and whose it is. `home` is what the clinician came to the screen to do — the call, the record, the visit — and is always first, one tap away from every tool. `tools` is the order the role reaches them in; `refused` is what that role is never granted, said where the doctor's tools would be, in a sentence that is MyThuso's rule rather than a claim about the law: on this platform a prescription, a sick note, a test and an onward referral are a doctor's. `from` is the visit stage the toolkit first appears at — a nurse is shown the patient's devices once the visit code has opened the visit, and not on the road. scripts/check-consultation-toolkit.mjs fails the build if a nurse surface ever lists a prescription or a sick note, if a refused tool's capability is ever granted to the role refusing it, or if a listed tool's capability is never granted to the role listing it.

gates.lineDoesNotAllow: The line does not allow a decision to be reached just now, so {tool} waits. What is written in it is kept, and it opens again when the line does.
gates.notAConsultation: This encounter did not count as a consultation, so nothing is decided from it here. {tool} stays closed for this appointment.
gates.notesDuringCall: Notes written during the call stay a draft until the call ends as a consultation. An interrupted encounter has no assessment, no plan and no signature, so nothing here is signed while the line is open.
gates.notOnFile: {patient} has no file in this preview’s records, so no file is shown. A tool never opens another patient’s file in place of this one.
gates.beingBuilt: {tool} is being built. When it lands it opens here, under the clinician’s registration and with its own refusals, like every other tool.
gates.notOnThisPhone: {tool} is written in the web workspace in this preview. On this phone it says what it is, who may use it and what it will not do, and opens nothing.
gates.notYetAtHandover: This visit is handed to a doctor once its readings are attached and signed off. It is at “{stage}” now, and the handover opens when the visit reaches it.

words.stateRoom: Needs the nurse in the room
words.rulesHeading: What these tools will not do
words.askedOf: Asked of the vetting register for {name} · {reference}
words.callDoctorLimits: What the doctor may do with you in the room

refusals.sentence: No tool here acts on its own. Each asks the clinician, says what it will not do in its own words, and sends nothing anywhere.
Opening a tool does not pause the call or change who is in the room. The line, the roster and every consent stay as they were, and the call is one tap away.
A tool never shows another patient’s file in place of this one. A patient with no file in this preview is said to have none.
A nurse is shown the patient’s devices from the moment the visit code opens the visit, and not on the road. She reads a patient’s readings in the house she was let into.
The patient never sees this toolkit. It is the clinician’s view of the consultation, and nothing in it reaches the patient unless a clinician writes it into the record.

_refusalsNote: What the toolkit itself will not do, beside the refusals each tool already carries. A refusal that names `surfaces` is said on those alone — the call goes on only where there is a call, and the devices wait for the door only where there is a door. The live board's refusals — no score, no device triage, no interpretation, no alarm, no heatmap — are packages/catalog/live-vitals.json's and are drawn by the board, not repeated here.
